rationale.conceptual: The underlying quantum chemical method (HF/STO-3G) is standard, but reproducing the paper's results requires building specific cluster models with constrained bond lengths and angles from a zeolite crystal structure and performing multiple constrained optimizations. Understanding the molecular geometry constraints and correctly implementing them in a quantum chemistry package demands non-trivial domain knowledge.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves setting up cluster geometries, running a few constrained SCF optimizations and a single-point calculation. The steps are sequential and can be accomplished with a single script using PySCF; no complex orchestration or external data dependencies beyond a crystal structure reference.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires reproducing HF/STO-3G energies for constrained cluster models of a silica active site. The method is standard computational chemistry, but the precise geometry constraints (fixing angles, bond lengths) and modeling of the distorted oxygen bridge demand careful implementation. Computational resource demands are negligible due to the small cluster size and cheap basis set.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Clusters contain only a few tens of atoms; HF/STO-3G calculations are very cheap (CPU minutes) and require minimal memory. No training or large data.
